assertion_results.text: States that jwt.decode does not verify the signature (token is forgeable) — distinct from just 'trusting the role claim'
assertion_results.evidence: "`jwt.decode()` only base64-decodes the token and never checks its signature or expiry."

assertion_results.text: Describes the exploit: forge/modify a token to role=admin (or alg=none) to bypass auth
assertion_results.evidence: "An attacker writes their own token with `{"role":"admin"}` (unsigned or with any signature), sends it as `Authorization`, and line 2 grants admin."

assertion_results.text: Fix: verify the signature with jwt.verify (key + expiry) before trusting any claim
assertion_results.evidence: "use `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'], issuer, audience })`... Rely on the built-in `exp`/`nbf` checks and reject the request on any error."

assertion_results.text: Rates it Critical/High and follows the exploit + impact + fix format
assertion_results.evidence: Listed under "🔴 Critical" with "Exploit:", "Impact: anyone can become admin without credentials", and "Fix:" bullets.
